identification.summary: Storm-0216 is Microsoft's name for a financially motivated ransomware operator that Microsoft associates with Twisted Spider and UNC2198 [S4][S5]. Proofpoint tracked TA2101 in late 2019, impersonating German, Italian and US government agencies to deliver Maze ransomware [S1][S2]. Mandiant's UNC2198 cluster covers IcedID-initiated intrusions that ended in Maze (July 2020) and Egregor (October 2020) deployment [S3]. In late 2023 Microsoft reported Storm-0216 hands-on-keyboard activity after Danabot infections, ending in Cactus ransomware [S4][S5].
identification.firstObserved: Proofpoint reported TA2101 campaigns between 16 October and 12 November 2019 [S1]. Mandiant created UNC2198 in June 2020 [S3].
identification.notes: Cluster boundaries differ by vendor: Proofpoint TA2101, Mandiant UNC2198 (which absorbed UNC2374 and UNC2414) and Microsoft Storm-0216 are mapped to one another by Microsoft and by press coverage [S3][S4][S5]. Mandiant says UNC2420 (Shathak/TA551) distributes the payloads UNC2198 used for access but treats it as a separate distribution cluster [S3]. Microsoft tracks Danabot as Storm-1044, a separate actor that hands off access [S4][S5].

attribution.sponsor: No state sponsor identified in the sources gathered; Mandiant describes UNC2198 as financially motivated [S3]. The source record lists country as RU; Microsoft is reported to describe Storm-0216 as Russia-based [S4].
attribution.confidence: Vendor assessments only. Mandiant assesses the objective is to monetize intrusions via ransomware and merged clusters through shared infrastructure and tooling, which it calls an analytical practice, not a definitive identity claim [S3]. Microsoft links Storm-0216 to Twisted Spider and UNC2198 [S4][S5].
attribution.basis: Shared Cobalt Strike team-server certificate (self-signed 'Oracle Inc', TCP 25055), WINDARC paths, code-signing certificate and RCLONE paths [S3]; Microsoft telemetry of Danabot-to-Storm-0216 handoff, as relayed in press coverage of Microsoft's posts [S4][S5]. Microsoft's original post was not opened.

objectives: Financial gain through ransomware and data-theft extortion; Mandiant states UNC2198 aims to monetize intrusions by compromising networks with ransomware [S3].

sectors: Business and IT services (2019 TA2101 recipients)
targeting.notes: Targeting is opportunistic across industries. Mandiant says UNC2198 victims were primarily in North America across a breadth of industries [S3]. 2019 campaigns are from Proofpoint and secondary coverage [S1][S2]. 2023 victim sectors were not stated in the sources gathered.

capabilities.summary: 2019: macro-laden Word lures impersonating government agencies running PowerShell to download Maze [S1]. 2020 (UNC2198): IcedID delivered via MOUSEISLAND and PHOTOLOADER, WINDARC TeamViewer-hijacking backdoor, SYSTEMBC proxy, Cobalt Strike BEACON in about 90% of intrusions, Metasploit, KOADIC, Empire, BloodHound, lateral movement by WinRM, RDP, PsExec and SMB BEACON, privilege escalation with a CVE-2020-0787 exploit, RCLONE exfiltration before encryption, and Maze or Egregor deployment (PsExec for Maze, forced GPO updates for Egregor) with time-to-ransom of 5.5 and 1.5 days respectively [S3]. 2023: access via Danabot (private build, malvertising) after QakBot disruption, RDP lateral movement, Cactus ransomware [S4][S5].

campaigns.name: TA2101 government-impersonation campaigns
campaigns.summary: Lures impersonating the German Federal Ministry of Finance (lookalike .icu sender domains, RSA SecurID-themed document) delivering Maze via macro-enabled Word documents and PowerShell [S1]; secondary coverage adds Italian Revenue Agency and USPS impersonation [S2]. Activity ran 16 October to 12 November 2019.

campaigns.name: UNC2198 ICEDID intrusion
campaigns.summary: Mandiant created UNC2198 from an ICEDID intrusion that compromised 32 systems in 26 hours without ransomware deployment.

campaigns.name: Maze deployment
campaigns.summary: An UNC2198 intrusion ended with Maze deployed via PsExec, 5.5 days after initial access.

campaigns.name: Egregor deployment
campaigns.summary: An UNC2198 intrusion ended with Egregor deployed via forced GPO updates, 1.5 days after access; Mandiant notes timing is consistent with Maze shutting down.

campaigns.name: Danabot to Cactus campaign
campaigns.summary: Microsoft reported Danabot (Storm-1044) infections, spread via malvertising since November 2023, handed off to Storm-0216 for hands-on-keyboard activity and Cactus deployment, after the August 2023 QakBot takedown.

diamond.adversary: Financially motivated ransomware operator tracked as TA2101, UNC2198, Twisted Spider and Storm-0216 [S1][S3][S4].
diamond.capability: Phishing macros, IcedID/Danabot access, Cobalt Strike, WINDARC, SYSTEMBC, RCLONE, Maze, Egregor, Cactus [S1][S3][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Cobalt Strike team servers with self-signed 'Oracle Inc' certificate on TCP 25055; lookalike .icu sender domains in Germany; malvertising delivery for Danabot [S1][S3][S5].
diamond.victim: Organizations in Germany, Italy and the US in 2019; North American organizations across industries in 2020 [S1][S3].
diamond.socioPolitical: Criminal extortion; ransomware operators monetize intrusions [S3].
diamond.technology: Windows domains reachable via phishing-delivered loaders, RDP, PsExec and GPO; BITS privilege escalation CVE-2020-0787 [S3].

gaps: Microsoft's original Storm-0216 post could not be opened; details rely on secondary coverage [S4][S5]. Proofpoint's post was seen in search results only, not opened in full [S1].
Whether TA2101, UNC2198 and Storm-0216 are one continuous group is a vendor mapping, not independently verified; Mandiant itself cautions its cluster merges are analytic judgments [S3].
Relationship between the Maze/Egregor operators and the 2023 Cactus activity is not established in sources gathered beyond the Microsoft mapping.
Victim counts, ransom figures and 2024-2026 activity were not found.
CrowdStrike Twisted Spider and Secureworks GOLD VILLAGE profiles listed in the record were not opened; aliases are unverified beyond the record.
Country attribution (RU) is from the source record; no primary evidence was reviewed.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Windows domain infrastructure, remote-access paths (RDP, TeamViewer-like tools) and email gateways at contractor and supporting organizations are relevant terrain; the actor is criminal, so effects fall on availability and data confidentiality [S3]. STEP 2: Time from access to ransom was 1.5 to 5.5 days in 2020, narrowing response windows [S3]. STEP 3: The template is phishing or malvertising, loader (IcedID/Danabot), Cobalt Strike, domain discovery, RCLONE exfiltration, then PsExec or GPO ransomware deployment [S3][S4]. STEP 4: MLCOA is opportunistic ransomware and extortion against commercial and supporting organizations. MDCOA is a ransomware outbreak against a DoD-supporting or healthcare-adjacent entity during a crisis, degrading mission support. Candidate indicators: rclone.exe in C:\PerfLogs, scheduled task named shadowdev, BEACON as int32.dll, new GPO pushes of executables, Danabot malvertising hits [S3][S4].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track commodity loader activity (IcedID, Danabot) as precursors, since handoffs to ransomware operators occur within days [S3][S4]. (2) Authorities: criminal activity against US companies is law-enforcement-led; coordinate defensive response through established DIB and law enforcement channels rather than assuming military authority. (3) Mission assurance: protect domain controllers and GPO integrity, keep offline backups, and restrict RDP and remote tools [S3]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with DC3/DIB partners and track takedown events (QakBot, August 2023) that cause actors to change tooling [S4].

provenance.importedSummary: Proofpoint researchers detected campaigns from a relatively new actor, tracked internally as TA2101, targeting German companies and organizations to deliver and install backdoor malware. The actor initiated their campaigns impersonating the Bundeszentralamt fur Steuern, the German Federal Ministry of Finance, with lookalike domains, verbiage, and stolen branding in the emails. For their campaigns in Germany, the actor chose Cobalt Strike, a commercially licensed software tool that is generally used for penetration testing and emulates the type of backdoor framework used by Metasploit, a similar penetration testing tool. Proofpoint researchers have also observed this actor distributing Maze ransomware, employing similar social engineering techniques to those it uses for Cobalt Strike, while also targeting organizations in Italy and impersonating the Agenzia Delle Entrate, the Italian Revenue Agency. We have also recently observed the actor targeting organizations in the United States using the IcedID banking Trojan while impersonating the United States Postal Service (USPS).
